66.text:
May 13, 2025
EBC 2025-1-073

Electoral Boundaries Commission

Dear Sirs:

I am concerned about the changes you are about to make in Alberta's electoral boundaries.

The new arrangement will no doubt give more power to urban voters and even less to rural ones, who are already so outnumbered that they can be conveniently ignored.

Also, some ridings, due to low population density, are extremely large, requiring excessive travel distances to serve all areas well.

I don't think population alone is a fair way to compare constituencies.

Concerning your previous such exercise: whoever decided how to divide the Medicine Hat riding did not have convenience in mind. Take, for example, twp. road 132 (to us, this is the Long Valley road). Residents on the south side are in the Irvine/Walsh community and vote in Irvine. Those on the north side, though part of the same community, are in the next constituency and vote in Schuler. Between them and Schuler is a large community pasture crossed by a rarely travelled side road. They never go to Schuler otherwise.

Likewise, residents of Graburn area, south of Walsh, are to vote in Elkwater - a direct summer road away, but indirect and distant by the highway route.

The people who make these decisions should consider that the terrain is not as flat as the map, and not all roads are the same.

[signed; the name is on the commission's published list for this number]
[address blacked out in source] Irvine, AB
